title: Grade 12 MUSIC AND DANCE — General Assessment #4

pages.quiz:
MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Brown, pink, and gold
   B. Black, white, and grey
   C. Green, orange, and purple
   D. Red, blue, and yellow

2. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. The speed of the music
   B. Only the volume
   C. The ticket price
   D. Only the costume

3. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   D. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. Best practice when working on Four-Part Harmony: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Four-Part Harmony.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Four-Part Harmony.
   C. Damage equipment used for Four-Part Harmony.
   D. Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. Best practice when working on Setting Text to Music: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Setting Text to Music.
   B. Damage equipment used for Setting Text to Music.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Setting Text to Music.
   D. Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.
   C. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.

7. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Guarantee a trophy
   B. Replace drinking water
   C. Remove the need for rules
   D. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

8. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   C. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.

9. Best practice when working on Kenyan Contemporary Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   C. Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Contemporary Songs.

10. Best practice when working on Dance Production: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Dance Production.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Dance Production.
   C. Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Dance Production.

11. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.
   B. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.
   D. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. Best practice when working on Western Instruments: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Western Instruments.
   B. Damage equipment used for Western Instruments.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Western Instruments.
   D. Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Music and Dance Industry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Instrumental Transpositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Setting Text to Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Red, blue, and yellow

2. A — The speed of the music

3. D — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. D — Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. D — Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. C — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. D — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

8. A — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. C — Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. C — Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. D — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. D — Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Music and Dance Industry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Rhythm; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Instrumental Transpositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Setting Text to Music; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
